post.caption:
Deep-sea ROVs work at pressures that crush a person instantly, nuclear decommissioning robots work in radiation that kills in minutes, and disaster response machines go where nobody can follow. But the hardest constraint on a Mars rover is none of that. It is delay: four to twenty-four minutes each way, so by the time you see the rock you have already hit it. A rover cannot be joysticked, which makes autonomy a requirement out there rather than a convenience.
